sections.title: How do I count in a smaller unit?
sections.label: Smaller
sections.intro: The measurement stays the same. Smaller units fit more times along it, so the number increases.

blocks.html: For length use 10 mm = 1 cm, 100 cm = 1 m and 1000 m = 1 km. For mass use 1000 g = 1 kg and 1000 kg = 1 t.

blocks.prompt: A cone of base radius 63 cm and vertical height 84 cm is cut parallel to its base. The removed cone has base radius 21 cm. Find the perpendicular height of the removed cone.

sections.title: How can I calculate the remaining volume?
sections.label: Volume
sections.intro: Use the similarity result for the small cone's perpendicular height. Then calculate two volumes using their own radii and heights.

blocks.html: Frustum volume is full-cone volume minus small-cone volume.

blocks.prompt: A cone of base radius 66 cm and vertical height 88 cm is cut parallel to its base. The removed cone has base radius 22 cm. Find the volume of the remaining solid. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
blocks.hint: Use similarity to find the small cone's height. Subtract its volume from the whole cone's volume.
blocks.solution:
Use similarity to find the small cone's height. Subtract its volume from the whole cone's volume.

\(\frac13\pi\left(66^2\times 88-22^2\times \frac{88}{3}\right)=\frac{1107392}{9}\pi\).

The result is \(\frac{1107392}{9}\pi\) cm³.

retry.feedback: The volume of the tip cone still needs to be subtracted.

blocks.html: A length scale factor must be cubed if you use it directly to scale a volume.

sections.title: Which areas form the frustum's skin?
sections.label: Skin
sections.intro: The original curved surface loses the small curved tip. The cut exposes a new small disc. The original base remains.

blocks.html: Subtract the two curved cone areas, then add both circular faces.

blocks.prompt: A cone of base radius 69 cm and vertical height 92 cm is cut parallel to its base. The removed cone has base radius 23 cm. The whole cone's slant height is 115 cm. Find the total surface area of the remaining frustum. Give your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
blocks.hint: Scale the slant height for the removed cone. Subtract its curved surface from the large cone's curved surface. Add both end discs.
blocks.solution:
Scale the slant height for the removed cone. Subtract its curved surface from the large cone's curved surface. Add both end discs.

\(\pi\left(69\times 115-23\times \frac{115}{3}+69^2+23^2\right)=\frac{37030}{3}\pi\).

The result is \(\frac{37030}{3}\pi\) cm².

retry.feedback: The smaller end is now a newly exposed flat circle. Include it.
